issue.title: Close button on notifications is read as "Dismiss" in French
issue.body:
One of our accountants uses VoiceOver with her Ledgerline profile set to French.
The text of the small notifications at the bottom of the page is read in French
("Fichier reçu. L'import va bientôt commencer."), but the close button on every
notification is announced as "Dismiss, button". The upload form and the date
range picker around it are read in French too.
## Discussion

### ben-ops (maintainer) · 2026-11-05
Thanks for the report. Is it every notification, or only the one after an upload?

### a11y-review-cm · 2026-11-05
Every one we've seen. The button looks the same (×); it's only what the
screen reader says.

input.title: Announce the toast close button in the user's locale
input.body:
File: src/components/Toast.tsx

The close button's aria-label calls t("ui.toast.dismiss") without a locale, so t() falls back to DEFAULT_LOCALE (en) and screen readers say "Dismiss" even though fr.json has "Fermer". Other components (UploadForm, DateRangePicker, ReportTable) pass `locale` as the third argument to t(). Give ToastProvider a locale prop (or otherwise supply the user's locale), pass it down to Toast, and call t("ui.toast.dismiss", {}, locale).

This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

Thanks for the detailed report; here is what triage found.

The close button's aria-label calls t("ui.toast.dismiss") without a locale, so it falls back to English even though fr.json already has "Fermer". The other components pass their locale to t(), and Toast has no locale to pass. I opened a draft PR (pr-6) that proposes passing the locale into the toast provider and using it for the label.

In short: the close button's aria-label calls t("ui.toast.dismiss") without a locale, so it falls back to English even though fr.json already has "Fermer".

This triage rests on the issue as it was filed and on what RepoMind's own reads of the repository returned. If any of it looks wrong, a maintainer can change the label or close the draft pull request. Nothing has been merged.
